text.en: Make a paper fan from a rectangular paper folded every 2 cm, with ice-cream sticks stuck on. Opening the fan a little or a lot shows different angles.

With the paper fan we keep one side fixed and turn the other. A small opening shows an acute angle, less than a quarter turn.
When the opening is exactly one quarter turn we get a right angle. More than a quarter turn but less than a half turn is an obtuse angle, and a half turn is a straight angle.
Two acute turns together may or may not be acute. Two small turns can add up to a right angle or even an obtuse angle.
Look at a house made from notebook covers. At the corners of the walls you can find right angles, and under the roof you will find acute and obtuse angles.
A turn bigger than a half turn is more than a straight angle. You can find angles in gymnasts' legs, the hands of a clock and open scissors.
Try this: draw a shape with 5 sides in your notebook that has 2 right angles, 2 obtuse angles and 1 acute angle.

problem.en: Name the angle made when a door opens a quarter turn.

text.en: A quarter of a full turn.
That is the same as the corner of a book.
So it is a right angle.

why.en: Less is acute, more is obtuse.

prompt.en: A friend says a clock at 3 o'clock shows a straight angle. What will you tell them?

requiredIdeas.en: At 3 the hands make a right angle
At 6 they make a straight line
A straight angle is a half turn

commonMisconceptions.en: Mixing up right angle and straight angle

points.en: Acute is less than a quarter turn.
Right angle is a quarter turn; obtuse is between a quarter and a half turn.
Straight angle is a half turn.
